question: Find the equation of the curve passing through $(1,1)$ if the slope of the tangent at any point $(x,y)$ on the curve is $$\frac{y-x}{x+y}.$$ Show that the resulting differential equation is homogeneous and obtain the required curve by a suitable substitution.
explanation:
Formation of Equation
The slope of the tangent at any point $(x,y)$ is $\frac{dy}{dx}$. Hence, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y-x}{x+y}.$$ Dividing the numerator and denominator on the right by $x$, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\frac{y}{x}-1}{1+\frac{y}{x}}.$$ Thus the right-hand side is a function of $\frac{y}{x}$ only, so the differential equation is homogeneous.

Applying the Substitution
Put $y=vx$. Then $$\frac{dy}{dx}=v+x\frac{dv}{dx}.$$ Therefore, $$v+x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{v-1}{1+v}.$$ Hence, $$x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{v-1-v-v^2}{1+v}=-\frac{1+v^2}{1+v}.$$ Separating the variables, $$\frac{1+v}{1+v^2}dv=-\frac{dx}{x}.$$

Evaluation
Integrating, $$\int\frac{dv}{1+v^2}+\int\frac{v}{1+v^2}dv=-\int\frac{dx}{x}.$$ Therefore, $$\tan^{-1}v+\frac{1}{2}\log(1+v^2)=-\log|x|+C.$$ Replacing $v$ by $\frac{y}{x}$ and simplifying the logarithmic terms gives $$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+\frac{1}{2}\log(x^2+y^2)=C.$$

The curve passes through $(1,1)$. Therefore, $$C=\tan^{-1}(1)+\frac{1}{2}\log 2=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{1}{2}\log 2.$$

Final Result
The required curve is $$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+\frac{1}{2}\log(x^2+y^2)=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{1}{2}\log 2.$$
